package_info.package_versions: All unpatched versions prior to September 2023 patch (CVE-2023-42793)
package_info.why_malicious: The entire package is considered compromised due to a critical remote code execution vulnerability (CVE-2023-42793) that allowed attackers to bypass authorization, execute arbitrary code, deploy persistent backdoors, and exfiltrate sensitive data. The compromise enabled attackers to weaponize the CI/CD pipeline, impacting downstream consumers and supply chain partners.

execution_context.file_location: TeamCity server process (arbitrary code execution context)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Arbitrary attacker-supplied code executed via RCE exploit (CVE-2023-42793). Example: attackers run PowerShell or bash payloads to download and execute further malware.
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: Upon exploitation, the code executes arbitrary commands on the TeamCity server, enabling download and execution of additional payloads, privilege escalation, and lateral movement.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Remote code execution on a CI/CD server is highly suspicious and enables full compromise.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal TeamCity operation should never allow unauthenticated remote code execution.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: None; only legitimate admin actions under strict authentication.
key_indicators: Unusual process launches from TeamCity context

execution_context.file_location: TeamCity server (malicious update or plugin, memory-resident payload)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Malicious payload disguised as a legitimate update or plugin, deployed in-memory or as a file, designed for data exfiltration and persistent access. Example: encrypted backdoor communicating with C2.
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: After gaining access, the code establishes persistence, exfiltrates sensitive data (credentials, code, user info), and maintains a covert channel to attacker infrastructure.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Payloads that establish persistence, exfiltrate data, and communicate with external C2 are classic indicators of compromise.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate TeamCity updates/plugins should not exfiltrate data or maintain covert channels.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Automated update checks (without exfiltration or persistence).
key_indicators: Network connections to untrusted external hosts

execution_context.file_location: TeamCity server memory or disk (malicious process or injected code)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Data harvesting and exfiltration logic: systematically collects proprietary code, credentials, and user data, then sends it to attacker-controlled infrastructure.
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code enumerates sensitive files and environment variables, packages them, and exfiltrates via HTTPS or other covert channels.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Harvesting and exfiltrating sensitive data is a hallmark of advanced persistent threats.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: CI/CD servers should not transmit internal data to untrusted external destinations.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: None; only legitimate telemetry (never sensitive data).
key_indicators: Bulk access to sensitive files (source code, credentials)
Outbound network traffic to attacker infrastructure

attack_chain.action: Exploit CVE-2023-42793 to gain remote code execution on TeamCity server.
Deploy malicious payload (backdoor or data exfiltration tool) disguised as legitimate update or plugin.
attack_chain.leads_to: Establish persistence and enable further malicious operations.

attack_chain.action: Harvest sensitive data (code, credentials, user info) and exfiltrate to attacker infrastructure.
attack_chain.leads_to: Compromise of organizational secrets and potential downstream supply chain impact.

attack_chain.action: Maintain long-term access and lateral movement within the network, potentially compromising additional systems.
attack_chain.leads_to: Broader organizational compromise and persistent threat presence.

behavioral_signatures: Unauthorized remote code execution on TeamCity server processes
Deployment of new or modified plugins/updates outside normal update channels
Unusual outbound network connections from CI/CD infrastructure
Bulk access to sensitive files and environment variables
file_indicators: Unexpected binaries or scripts in TeamCity plugin/update directories
Memory-resident payloads with obfuscated or encrypted content
Unauthorized modifications to TeamCity configuration files
network_indicators: Outbound HTTPS or other protocol connections to untrusted or attacker-controlled domains/IPs
C2 infrastructure used for persistence and data exfiltration
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor TeamCity server logs for signs of unauthorized code execution, plugin installation, or update activity. Alert on outbound network connections to untrusted destinations, especially following privilege escalation events. Use EDR/XDR to detect memory-resident payloads and anomalous process launches. Audit for bulk access to sensitive files and environment variables by TeamCity processes. Correlate with known indicators of compromise for CVE-2023-42793 exploitation.
